tse.name: Cloud TSE
tse.description: Signs every till transaction under the German KassenSichV – required for cash in Germany.
tse.longDescription: In Germany, a till that accepts cash needs a certified technical security device (TSE) that signs every transaction. OpenEOS connects the Swissbit Cloud TSE 2 for this: one TSE per organization, your devices act as terminals of one shared till. As soon as a paid event is coming up, the TSE is set up automatically; receipts then carry the TSE data with a QR code, and the data is exported and archived every night. With an active TSE you can choose the operating mode “All features” with cash. The TSE runs for the month of your event and is deactivated automatically at the end of the month. More in the <link>FAQ on openeos.de</link>.

de.title: Till rules in Germany
de.text: In Germany a till that can record cash needs a certified TSE (KassenSichV). That is why “All features” with cash is only available with an active cloud TSE (Integrations → Cloud TSE). In “Orders only” and “Cashless” OpenEOS records no cash; you get a manufacturer certificate for your records.
de.textComingSoon: In Germany a till that can record cash needs a certified TSE (KassenSichV). That's why “All features” with cash is only available with an active cloud TSE – which is coming soon. Until then you can use “Orders only” or “Cashless”: OpenEOS records no cash there, and you get a manufacturer's certificate for your records.

at.title: Cash register obligation in Austria
at.text: In Austria the cash register obligation (RKSV) applies from €15,000 annual turnover per business if more than €7,500 of it is cash turnover. Note: card payments count as cash turnover in Austria – this also applies in “Cashless”. OpenEOS currently creates no RKSV signature. Exemptions exist, for example, for small festivals of non-profit clubs of up to 72 hours per calendar year and for canteens of non-profit clubs up to €45,000 annual turnover (net, on at most 52 days a year; limit since 2026). Check the rules for your club yourself or with your tax advisor – whichever operating mode you choose.

ch.title: Note for Switzerland
ch.text: To our knowledge, Switzerland has no general cash register or fiscalization obligation. All three operating modes are available to you. Record-keeping and VAT rules still apply to clubs. Check yourself or with your fiduciary or tax advisor what applies to your club.

other.title: Till rules in your country
other.text: Many countries have their own rules for tills (e.g. Italy, France, Poland, Czechia). All three operating modes are available to you – check yourself whether OpenEOS and the chosen operating mode are permissible for you there.
